# Results — Study 225 (Sector-Rotation) on real monthly ETF tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Strategy: rotate monthly into the
top-3 SPDR sector ETFs ranked by trailing 6-month total return (6-1 momentum convention).
Universe: 11 SPDR sector ETFs. Benchmarks: equal-weight sector basket, SPY, and a
random-rotation control (50 seeds). As-of **2026-06-16**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Tickers | N months | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|--:|---|
| Yahoo (yfinance, auto_adjust=True) | 1993-02 → 2026-06 | 11 sector ETFs + SPY | 401 | `a6bfb5f255da` |

Key tickers and their earliest month-end: XLB/XLE/XLF/XLI/XLK/XLP/XLU/XLV/XLY start
**1998-12** (but the first full return month is 1999-01); XLRE launched **2015-10**;
XLC (Communication Services) launched **2018-06**.

## The honest test — top-3 momentum vs equal-weight and random-rotation (gross, cost=0)

| Arm | N months | Ann. return | Ann. vol | Sharpe | Max drawdown | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Momentum top-3 (6mo)** | 401 | **+7.8%** | 13.2% | **+0.59** | −41.5% | **+3.46** |
| Equal-weight sector basket | 401 | +7.7% | 13.4% | +0.58 | −43.0% | +3.38 |
| Random-rotation (50 seeds, mean) | 401 | +7.6% | — | — | — | — |
| **SPY benchmark** | 401 | **+11.4%** | 14.8% | **+0.77** | −50.8% | **+4.44** |

**Active return vs EW:** +0.1%/yr, Sharpe +0.01, HAC *t* = **+0.09** — indistinguishable from
zero. The 6-month sort adds nothing above merely holding all sectors equally.

**Active return vs SPY:** −3.7%/yr, HAC *t* = **−2.12** — significantly *worse* than the cap-
weighted index. Equal-sector-weighting itself already underperforms SPY by ~3.6%/yr; the
momentum sort does not rescue this gap.

## Sub-period stability — performance is inconsistent

| Period | Mom ann. | Mom Sharpe | HAC *t* | EW Sharpe | Active (mom − EW) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1999–2009** | +4.4% | +0.30 | +0.90 | +0.28 | +0.2% |
| **2010–2019** | +12.3% | +1.11 | +3.93 | +1.16 | **−0.5%** (EW wins) |
| **2020–2026** | +11.6% | +0.81 | +2.35 | +0.93 | **−1.3%** (EW wins) |

The 2010s and 2020s saw strong absolute returns — but the **equal-weight basket beat or
matched the momentum sort in both periods**. The sector sort adds nothing over the
trivial benchmark, and the full-period t-stat on the active return is +0.09.

## Cost sweep — the Sharpe survives costs, but active return doesn't

At the natural monthly rebalance cadence (ETF bid-ask ~ 3-10 bps round-trip):

| Round-trip cost | Net ann. return | Net Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | +7.8% | +0.59 | +3.46 |
| 5 bps | +7.5% | +0.57 | +3.34 |
| 10 bps | +7.2% | +0.55 | +3.21 |
| 20 bps | +6.6% | +0.50 | +2.96 |
| 40 bps | +5.5% | +0.42 | +2.46 |

The absolute Sharpe survives cost because the strategy is long equities. However, the
*active* return vs the EW benchmark was +0.1%/yr gross — any cost turns it negative.

## Lookback sensitivity (k=3, 0 cost)

| Lookback (months) | Ann. return | Sharpe | HAC *t* | Active Sharpe vs EW |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 3 | +7.0% | +0.56 | +3.15 | −0.03 |
| 6 | +7.8% | +0.59 | +3.46 | +0.01 |
| 9 | +7.0% | +0.54 | +3.11 | −0.04 |
| 12 | +7.9% | +0.60 | +3.52 | +0.02 |

Across all lookback windows the active Sharpe vs EW hovers near zero (range: −0.04 to +0.02).
The signal does not improve with lookback tuning.

## K sensitivity (6mo, 0 cost)

| K (top sectors) | Ann. return | Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2 | +8.2% | +0.56 | +3.45 |
| 3 | +7.8% | +0.59 | +3.46 |
| 4 | +7.8% | +0.61 | +3.57 |
| 5 | +7.8% | +0.62 | +3.65 |

Increasing K converges toward the EW basket — confirming the sector-sort contribution
shrinks to zero as portfolio concentration decreases.

## Synthetic positive control

On a deterministic synthetic panel with baked-in persistent cross-sector drifts
(`mom_strength=0.04, phi=0.92`), the 6-month sort earns a large active return vs
random rotation (planted signal detected cleanly). On the null (`mom_strength=0.0`),
active return vs random ≈ 0. The machinery works; the real tape has essentially no
exploitable cross-sector drift above the market factor.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The absolute HAC *t* is +3.46 over 26 years, but this is equity beta
  from being long sectors. The *active* return vs equal-weight is only +0.1%/yr with
  *t* = +0.09 — statistically zero. No lookback (3, 6, 9, 12 months) produces a meaningful
  active edge. WEAK is generous; NONE would also be defensible.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The momentum rotation consistently *underperforms* SPY by
  ~3.6%/yr (active *t* = −2.12). Equal-sector weighting already destroys cap-weight alpha;
  the momentum sort adds no further value. A practitioner would do better just buying SPY.
- **3rd axis — Survivorship:** XLC and XLRE have shorter histories (2018, 2015); the
  early-period universe had only 9 sectors. Results with fewer tickers would be similar
  given the active return is near zero across all subsets.
